## Europe in 2020

As of 2020, Europe counted 749,524,044 inhabitants. That is 1.5% more than in 2010, when the population stood at 738,145,318.

The median age was 42.5 years, and for every 100 people of working age (15–64) there were 24.4 children under 15 and 29.3 people aged 65 or over. The narrow base of the pyramid marks a constrictive age structure: fertility below replacement level and a rising share of older people.

Frequently asked questions about Europe's population

How many people lived in Europe in 2020? Europe had a population of 749,524,044 in 2020.

What is the median age in Europe?

The median age in Europe is 42.5 years — half the population is younger, half older.

How many children and older people live in Europe?

In Europe, 15.9% of people are under 15 and 19.1% are 65 or older.

What type of population pyramid does Europe have?

Europe has a constrictive pyramid: cohorts of children are smaller than those of their parents, reflecting low fertility and an ageing population.
